title: SSO & RBAC operationalizing workshop w/ Crimson Analytics
topics: SAML SSO setup and IdP mapping
RBAC least-privilege model and role slices
summary: Redwood AE/SE ran a focused security and integration workshop to review SSO (SAML) mappings, SCIM provisioning attributes, recommend a least-privilege RBAC model for Crimson's teams, and validate KMS/encryption options plus audit-log retention. Action items include SCIM mapping template, SOC2 + network docs, and scheduling a short pilot to validate SSO+RBAC behavior in a dedicated environment.
next_steps: Alex to send SOC2 + ISO artifacts and network architecture doc (links)
Priya to share SCIM attribute mapping template and role-slice playbook
Schedule 2-week pilot on Dedicated capacity for SSO/RBAC flows
Customer to confirm compliance audit window and list of auditors

Maya Lin (IAM) - provide IdP metadata (SAML) and test account for pilot - due 2026-08-14
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-12 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Tom Becker (CISO - Crimson), Maya Lin (IAM Engineer), Sara Holt (Platform Lead)

00:00 Alex (AE): ok hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a sec, um today is focused on SSO and RBAC operational patterns and making sure this maps to your compliance needs. quick round robin?
00:12 Tom (CISO): Tom here, we are primarily looking at least-privilege, audit trails for SOC 2 and ISO, and ensuring our IdP integration doesn't leak PII. timeline is Q3 compliance review.
00:23 Maya (IAM): Maya — we run Okta, have SCIM already but attribute mappings are messy across teams.
00:31 Sara (Platform): Sara, platform team — concerned about service accounts and machine-to-machine tokens; also curious about private deployment options.
00:40 Priya (SE): Great, thanks. I'll be the technical lead for the redwood side; will go over SAML assertions, SCIM mapping and RBAC examples. Alex will cover compliance docs and next steps.
01:05 Alex (AE): Quick note we have SOC2 Type II artifacts and an ISO 27001 summary; I'll share links after the call. Also we'll include our audit log export blueprint.
01:22 Speaker 1: question — do you want us to start with SSO mapping or RBAC?
01:27 Tom (CISO): SSO first please, because provisioning ties into roles.

02:05 Priya (SE): ok SAML high-level — Redwood supports IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows, SAML 2.0. We usually consume x509 cert metadata and support let's say authn context mapping, nameid transient/persistent, and attributes.
02:34 Maya (IAM): for us we prefer persistent NameID, and we need email, uid, groups in the assertion.
02:48 Priya (SE): good — groups are important for our SCIM mapping but for SAML we can also pass group membership as an attribute. small caveat is that large group lists can bloat assertions. we typically recommend SCIM for sync and SAML for authn only.
03:10 Sara (Platform): do you have an example attribute list?
03:15 Priya (SE): yes — typical SAML attributes: email, fullName, uid, groups, orgUnit, roleHint. i'll send a template. note: some IdPs call groups 'memberOf' which we sometimes see transcribed incorrectly in exports.

04:00 Alex (AE): quick compliance note: for SOC2 we retain detailed audit logs for 90 days by default in hosted, with export options to your SIEM or to S3 for longer retention. for Dedicated/Private we can keep logs within your VPC and align retention with your policy.
04:26 Tom (CISO): retention to meet our policy — 1 year of detailed events, 7 years of high-level metadata, is that feasible?
04:38 Alex (AE): yes — for Dedicated we can support 1 year. Hosted would need an add-on long-term log retention or export to your archive. we'll include options in the package.

06:02 Priya (SE): moving to SCIM — we support SCIM 2.0, incremental delta syncs, and full sync. Our recommended mapping is to push users and groups from Okta into Redwood with attributes: userName, externalId, displayName, emails[type=work], active, roles (custom extension), and group membership as groups[].
06:28 Maya (IAM): which attribute do you use to map to RBAC roles? we have separate group sources for engineering and analytics.
06:36 Priya (SE): good question. We implemented extensions like urn:redwood:role to carry role slices (like analytics-readonly, infra-admin). Many customers prefer to map Okta groups to role slices in Redwood, then have platform-level roles that combine those slices.
07:01 Sara (Platform): can you demonstrate a sample role slice?
07:08 Priya (SE): sure — example: roleSlice: analytics-readonly -> grants: generate-embeddings, query-logs (read only), no model management. infra-admin slice -> allocate capacity, change deployment config. these are additive; then you define RBAC roles like 'Analyst' = [analytics-readonly], 'InfraOps' = [infra-admin, analytics-readonly].
07:36 Tom (CISO): ok how does least-privilege rollout look? we don't want everyone to have deploy rights.
07:44 Priya (SE): stepwise: 1) start with read-only slices to a pilot group; 2) freeze model management ops to a small admin group; 3) use canary rollouts and audit logs to detect unusual activity; 4) progressively expand with periodic attestation.
08:10 Maya (IAM): attestation — do you provide an access review report?
08:14 Alex (AE): yes we can generate periodic access reports per role and export CSVs for auditors. we'll show sample during pilot.

09:00 Speaker 2: concerning encryption — what's the story for KMS?
09:05 Priya (SE): Redwood supports customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS integrations for Private and Dedicated. For hosted, we offer KMS-integration per enterprise contracts where you can bring keys or we hold them depending on compliance. Encryption at rest is AES-256, in transit is TLS 1.2/1.3.
09:34 Tom (CISO): we need HSM-backed keys and a key rotation policy that we control.
09:40 Priya (SE): HSM-backed KMS is supported (we integrate with common cloud KMS/HSMs). rotation can be driven by your KMS policy; we do support key rollover workflows. one mis-note: for ephemeral KV cache encryption we might call it KV cash in some logs — sorry for that typo in docs.
10:10 Sara (Platform): for Private deployment, what network egress do you need? we run a locked-down VPC with strict egress rules.
10:18 Priya (SE): for Private, the control plane can be in your VPC so egress is internal. for hosted we need specific outbound endpoints for telemetry and updates — we will provide a port/hostname whitelist. Alex will share the network doc.

11:42 Maya (IAM): SCIM speed — if we have 10k users, how do delta syncs behave? we want predictable windows.
11:50 Priya (SE): we do incremental delta and full syncs during low load. for 10k users, delta cycles are quick; for full syncs we suggest scheduling during off-hours and using pagination. we'll show performance numbers in the playbook.
12:20 Tom (CISO): audit logs — do logs include token-level request traces and model inference metadata? we need to know PII leakage risk.
12:32 Priya (SE): logs include request-level metadata (timestamp, model id, token counts, route, user id if present) but by default not full payloads for privacy. We have options to capture request/response bodies for debug in a controlled way with retention limits and redaction. Many customers send full logs to their SIEM for short debugging windows.
13:10 Tom (CISO): we will want redaction controls and a policy for how long raw payloads persist.
13:17 Priya (SE): agreed — in Dedicated we can keep raw payloads inside your VPC and set retention to your policy. Hosted will require export or short retention.

14:05 Alex (AE): circling back — what is your preferred model for pilot? hosted or dedicated?
14:13 Sara (Platform): prefer dedicated for the pilot if cost is reasonable. we want to validate SCIM and SAML at scale plus role enforcement.
14:23 Alex (AE): ok Dedicated pilot it is. we'll propose a 2-week window with a small capacity pool and telemetry.

15:00 Priya (SE): deployment plan for pilot: 1) provision Dedicated pool; 2) pair Okta SCIM connector to dev tenant; 3) set up SAML test app; 4) seed role slices and map Okta groups; 5) run acceptance tests for role enforcement and audit exports.
15:28 Maya (IAM): for acceptance tests do you have scripts?
15:33 Priya (SE): yes — we'll share a test harness with scenarios: user_provision, group_change_provision, login_flow_assertion, role_sudo_attempt, audit_export_check. note: sometimes assertions fail due to clock skew — check NTP.

17:00 Speaker 3: what about service accounts? we don't want them to bypass RBAC.
17:07 Priya (SE): service accounts can be created with scoped roles and short-lived tokens. recommended: create machine roles with least privilege, rotate tokens, and bind audit events to service account ids. we also support OAuth-like tokens with TTL.
17:35 Tom (CISO): do you support JIT (just-in-time) provisioning for contractors?
17:40 Priya (SE): we can do JIT in combination with SCIM for full accounts; JIT simplifies access for occasional users but for full role attribution SCIM is more reliable.

19:00 Sara (Platform): compliance questions — auditors often ask about segregation of duties and admin access. how granular can you make admin boundaries?
19:12 Priya (SE): very granular — we have admin scopes: billing, deployments, model management, user provisioning, audit-read. You can combine or separate scopes as needed.
19:28 Alex (AE): we'll include a role matrix sample that maps to your internal SoD requirements.

20:30 Maya (IAM): edge case — what happens if SCIM and SAML disagree (e.g., SCIM says user removed but SAML assertion still active)?
20:40 Priya (SE): good edge case — our session validation checks user active state at login; SCIM removals mark user inactive and subsequent SAML logins fail. However long-lived sessions may persist until TTL expires. we suggest short session TTLs for high-sensitivity orgs.
21:05 Tom (CISO): what's the shortest session TTL you support?
21:10 Priya (SE): tokens down to 15 minutes for interactive sessions; service tokens shorter as needed.

22:00 Alex (AE): let's talk data residency — do you have a region requirement?
22:08 Tom (CISO): yes EU-only for certain datasets and US for others. we'll need a split-residency approach.
22:18 Priya (SE): we support region pinning and can route requests based on customer config; for Dedicated you can choose where the compute nodes reside. audit logs can be stored in-region or exported to your regional S3 buckets.

23:30 Sara (Platform): about the rollout, we want a phased approach: dev -> staging -> prod, with automated test gates. can Redwood integrate with our CI/CD?
23:41 Priya (SE): yes — we have API endpoints and Terraform modules for deployment config. can integrate with pipeline gates and make config changes via API.

25:00 Speaker 1: question on tooling — does Redwood provide an admin console for role management?
25:06 Priya (SE): yes web console + API. Console shows role slices, attached policies, activity logs and allows SCIM sync status checks.

26:10 Tom (CISO): how do you handle emergency access (break glass)?
26:16 Alex (AE): we support emergency roles with full audit and time-limited elevation with approval workflow. recommended pattern: create break-glass role with MFA enforced and record all sessions.
26:40 Maya (IAM): approval workflow — does it integrate with our ticketing (Jira)?
26:45 Priya (SE): we have webhooks and can call a webhook to your ticketing system; some customers integrate via a small lambda.

28:00 Sara (Platform): logging details — can you show a sample line from audit log?
28:07 Priya (SE): yes — sample: {timestamp, event_type, principal_id, action, resource, outcome, route, model_id, token_count} note: in the transcript we sometimes display curly braces — in the actual log we push JSON lines.
28:34 Tom (CISO): do logs include IP addresses?
28:38 Priya (SE): yes by default; we can redact IPs for privacy but auditors usually want them included.

30:00 Alex (AE): Pricing quick check — Dedicated pilot costs are a monthly pro-rated charge plus small setup. We'll give exact numbers in follow-up. You mentioned cost comparisons to BigCloudAI?
30:12 Tom (CISO): yes we ran a quick calc — need to weigh latency, data control, and price.
30:20 Alex (AE): understood. Dedicated gives you the most control and predictable throughput; hosted is cheaper to start but requires more add-ons for retention and KMS.

31:40 Priya (SE): operational quirk — when you use group-based SCIM to role mapping, be careful with group nesting. Okta nested groups can cause double membership; we recommend explicit flat groups for mapping.
31:58 Maya (IAM): we'll flatten for the pilot.

33:00 Sara (Platform): any known limitations re: large assertions or SCIM rate limits?
33:07 Priya (SE): SCIM rate limits are in the docs; for large orgs we can increase quotas during sync windows. assertions larger than ~64KB may cause some IdP trouble; better to keep group lists out of assertions for large groups.

34:20 Tom (CISO): auditability: can we have chain-of-custody for key rotations? auditors ask for proof who rotated keys when.
34:30 Priya (SE): yes — KMS logs plus Redwood admin audit events are correlated; we can provide rotation event logs with operator id, timestamp, and key id.

36:00 Alex (AE): ok let's capture concrete next steps and owners. Priya will send the SCIM+SAML templates and sample role-slice mapping. Alex will send SOC2 artifact pack, private network whitelist doc, and Dedicated pricing. Tom to confirm compliance calendar and provide IdP metadata to Maya.
36:25 Tom (CISO): will do. Also want to get a short list of required ports and endpoints for the firewall team.
36:33 Alex (AE): included in the network doc.

38:00 Priya (SE): quick demo note — when you run the pilot we'll run acceptance tests and give you an automated report that highlights mismatches (e.g., group mapping failure, provisioning errors).
38:12 Sara (Platform): great. who is the single point of contact for the pilot?
38:17 Alex (AE): Alex will be commercial lead, Priya technical. we'll cc a solutions engineer for the run.

40:00 Maya (IAM): a couple of small questions — which attributes map to email vs username?
40:07 Priya (SE): userName maps to the Okta 'login' attribute by default; we accept email as userName too, but be consistent. externalId should be your Okta user id for stable mapping.

41:30 Tom (CISO): anything we should watch out for in the SOC2 package re: vendor management?
41:37 Alex (AE): our vendor management section lists subprocessors and our third-party audits; we'll highlight the parties that may see telemetry during hosted mode.

43:00 Speaker 1: last quick operational piece — how long does it take to get Dedicated provisioned?
43:06 Priya (SE): typically 3-5 business days for a small pilot capacity, depending on quota approvals and networking. on-prem/private longer due to packaging.

44:20 Alex (AE): okay wrapping up — recap of immediate actions: send docs, set pilot dates, share IdP metadata. Any final questions?
44:31 Tom (CISO): no, thanks — this was helpful.
44:36 Sara (Platform): thanks everyone.
44:40 Alex (AE): thanks all, we'll follow up by tomorrow with the artifact links.
47:00 Meeting end.
